title: Concord product-reachability exception manifest
description: Closed contract for functions that no cmd/concord invocation can reach and that the repository has nonetheless decided to keep. Reachability is computed rather than declared (CD-0047 D4): scripts/check-reachability.py runs the pinned analysis, subtracts these exceptions, and fails on any remainder, so there is no per-symbol manifest to maintain and no way for the manifest to disagree with the code. A declared function that has become reachable is equally a finding, because stale exceptions widen the surface without anyone choosing to widen it. States reuse the vocabulary accepted in contracts/floor-readiness.schema.json, less 'satisfied': a reachable function is not an exception.

analysis.description: The pinned command that computes the finding set. Pinning the version is what makes the set reproducible: a toolchain upgrade then surfaces as a reviewable manifest diff rather than an unexplained CI failure. The tool runs through go run and is not a module dependency, the precedent .github/workflows/ci.yml already sets for govulncheck.

entrypoints.description: The complete set of program entrypoints. The OpenCode adapter reaches Go only by executing the binary, so cmd/concord is the whole product surface.

state.description: out_of_scope: an accepted decision keeps this unreachable, and it is declared rather than excused. outstanding: it should be reachable and is not, tracked by an issue. unmeasured: its status has not been assessed. One exception may cover several functions where a single decision governs them, because that is how the reasons cluster.

functions.description: Symbols as <package>.<Name>, where Name may carry a receiver. Line and column are deliberately excluded: the identity being declared is the function, not its position in a file.

issue.description: Public issue tracking an outstanding exception. Required when outstanding; forbidden otherwise.

reason.description: Why this is unmeasured or out of scope. Required for those states; forbidden otherwise.
